correctness.rationale: The normalized Beta-ball second and fourth moments reconstruct the exact degree-two kernel and its four orthogonal summands. Independent Gaussian and Gamma representations establish L1 and almost-sure convergence of the radial and angular terms uniformly in evaluation radius, so the Lebesgue function converges to a continuous convex Gamma–chi-square absolute moment. Gamma additivity with a Beta conditional law gives the strict center-constant monotonicity; chi-square-one at k=1/2 identifies the unique crossing, and independence with opposite signs proves strict interior convexity and the limit-point classification. Boundary evaluation matches the essential norm because the measure has full ball support. Replaying the actual checker returned 308 exact and finite diagnostics; analytic proof rather than experiments supplies the infinite-dimensional assertions.

value.rationale: Orthogonal polynomial projection of bounded data is a natural least-squares stability problem. The result computes its sharp degree-two dimensional growth constant for all fixed Jacobi radial weights and locates where amplification concentrates. A sharp transition at alpha=-1/2 separates a Gamma-driven radial instability at the center from a Gaussian angular instability at the boundary, information absent from generic polynomial approximation bounds. It yields precise positivity-loss sensitivity of the canonical projector without asserting global finite-dimensional formulas or higher-degree generality.
